name: itsukis-chat-hub
description: Itsuki's Chat Hub - a Discord-style client served as plain static files from GitHub. The SITE NEEDS NO BUILD STEP: index.html fetches the stylesheets and js/loader.js loads the scripts listed in js/manifest.js, in that order, into one shared global scope. This package.json exists only so the test and migration tooling is reproducible, and - since v54.6 - so the handful of things that used to live in loose markdown files are kept somewhere that ships with the code. See "comments".

comments.no-build-step: Visitors load index.html, which fetches css/ and js/ directly. Do not introduce a bundler, a framework or an install step for ordinary visitors. dist/index.single.html is an OPTIONAL one-file copy of the same app, produced by `npm run build:single`; it is a build OUTPUT, never the source.
comments.load-order: js/manifest.js is the one list of what loads and in what order. index.html carries its own copy of the CSS list (it has to - the stylesheets come from the raw repo and browsers refuse to apply them through <link>); the two MUST stay identical. Adding a file means adding it to BOTH.
comments.deploy:
Order matters.
1. ROTATE THE TWO EXPOSED CREDENTIALS if that has not been done. Both were once served in js/core/config.js and in dist/index.single.html, so they are in the GitHub history and are compromised; removing them from the code does not un-publish them. (a) Nyckel: delete the old client in the Nyckel dashboard, create a new one, and set NYCKEL_CLIENT_ID / NYCKEL_CLIENT_SECRET / NYCKEL_FUNCTION_ID as Vercel environment variables. The client id is not a secret and may also go in js/core/config.js; the SECRET never goes back into any file the browser is served. (b) Discord: delete the old webhook, create a new one, set DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL in Vercel. Confirm with `node test/security/no-secrets.js`.
2. Run the suites: `npm test` (offline) and `npm run test:browser` (needs Chrome).
3. Stamp the build: `BUILD_SECRET=<same value as in Vercel> node tools/stamp-build.js`, then set MIN_BUILD in Vercel to the label it prints. This is what kills every older open tab.
4. Rebuild the single file: `npm run build:single`.
5. Push the site files to GitHub.
6. PUBLISH THE DATABASE RULES - see "rules" below.
7. Deploy the api/ folder to Vercel if it is not already there. GitHub can only serve static files; api/ is server code (TOS logging, IP bans, the spin, NSFW scanning, username login). The site calls it over the internet, so hosting the pages from GitHub is not a problem.
comments.rules:
v54.7 CHANGES THE DATABASE RULES AND THEY MUST BE PUBLISHED. Two features stop working without them: a site owner deleting a server (one atomic multi-path write - a single refused path takes the whole delete down), and the owner control center's server list.
WHAT TO PUBLISH: the contents of firebase-rules.json, into Firebase console -> Realtime Database -> Rules -> Publish. firebase-rules.min.json is the same document minified (some consoles reject the pretty-printed size); the two MUST parse to identical objects - test/security/rules-audit.js fails the build if they drift. Regenerate with `npm run rules:minify`.
WHAT v54.6 CHANGED: scripts/add_rules_owner_delete.py restored the site owner's branch-level DELETE grant on servers, serverChannels, serverRoles, serverMembers, serverBans, serverMutes, serverIpBans, invites, serverEvents, serverEmoji, memberScreen and roomMembers. Every one is delete-only (!newData.exists()), so it is the power to remove a server, not to rewrite anybody's data.
WHAT v54.7 ADDED (scripts/add_rules_v547.py): (1) customroleLog/ - site-owner read, write FALSE for every client; api/customrole.js appends it with the Admin SDK. (2) serverDiscovery/$sid/cat and /tags validators, inheriting the listing's existing staff-only write rule. (3) servers/.read and serverMembers/.read for SITE OWNERS ONLY. That third one is the only read that was widened, and it adds enumeration and no new content: each child of both was ALREADY readable by every signed-in account, so a site owner could already fetch every one of these records individually. The full reasoning is written out in that script, and rules-audit.js requires every branch-level read grant to be documented with a reason before it will pass.
ROLLBACK: firebase-rules.v54-original.json is a byte-for-byte copy of the rules v54 shipped. Rules are not data - publishing them cannot change, move or delete a record; the worst case is an operation being refused.
comments.setup: Optional subsystems, each off until you configure it. FILE UPLOADS: Firebase Storage rules plus the `files` rule in the database rules; with no Blaze plan, fill in the Cloudinary fields in js/core/config.js instead and uploads go there. VOICE: Agora - set CFG.APP_ID and CFG.TOKEN_URL in js/core/config.js; with no token endpoint the project must have its App Certificate disabled. CUSTOM ROLES: customroles/ is world-readable and .write:false for every client on purpose, so roles are granted from the Firebase console or through api/totmilestone.js - never from the browser. MVP/VIP GRANTS: need the MVP rules published or the write is refused. NSFW SCANNING: needs api/nsfw.js deployed and the Nyckel environment variables set. TRICK-OR-TREAT: the rules allow only the one rate-limited write shape; awards go through api/totaward.js, which is idempotent. GLOBAL CUSTOM ROLES (v54.7): customroles/ is ".write": false for every client with no exception for owners - that is the security property, not an oversight. api/customrole.js is the only writer besides api/totmilestone.js; it verifies the caller's ID token and checks owners//secretowner/ with an admin read. It grants and revokes EXISTING roles and deliberately cannot create one, so a typo cannot become a permanent junk role - define roles in the Firebase console. Timed grants store an expiry at customroles/<role>/expires/<id>; members/<id> is unchanged, so every existing grant keeps working. DIAGNOSTICS: GET /api/health reports which environment variables are set, as booleans only. .env.example lists every variable the api/ folder actually reads, with placeholder values.
comments.security: Accepted risks are listed, each with its reasoning, at the end of test/security/attack-suite.js, and the suite prints them on every run. They SUCCEED BY DESIGN - a run reporting them is not a run that failed. The headline ones: the spin and several other economies are scored in the browser, because moving them server-side would break accounts that already exist; the real fix is server-side scoring. NEVER put a secret in js/, css/, index.html or dist/ - `node test/security/no-secrets.js` fails the build if one reappears. Site ownership is read from owners/$id and secretowner/$id in the database and from nowhere else: not a username, not localStorage, not a profile field, not a self-assigned role. Both the client and the rules test those same two nodes.
comments.testing:
FOUR different kinds of confidence. Conflating them is how "all tests pass" comes to mean less than it sounds like.
1. `npm test` - 10 offline suites, 1080 checks. Rules via TARGARYEN, an INDEPENDENT implementation of the rules language, NOT Google's evaluator. Strong evidence, not proof. Needs `npm install`.
2. `npm run test:browser` - 24 suites in a real Chromium against test/fake-firebase.js, an in-page stand-in for the database. Proves what the CLIENT does: which paths it writes, what the DOM shows, what it refuses. The fake has NO rules engine, so a write these suites watch succeed would also 'succeed' if the real rules forbade it. Needs Chrome.
3. `npm run test:api` - the api/ handlers over REAL HTTP on 127.0.0.1, with NO environment variables set. That is the configuration nobody tests and the most valuable one: a fresh deployment. 117 checks covering the method gate, CORS preflight, malformed and oversized bodies, rate limiting, and that every endpoint reports 'unconfigured' rather than pretending to have done its job. Also asserts that GET /api/health leaks no part of a secret even when the values exist.
4. `npm run test:emulator` - the rules against GOOGLE'S OWN evaluator (Firebase Emulator Suite), reading the same firebase-rules.json that gets published. THIS SUITE HAS NEVER BEEN EXECUTED: it was written in an environment that cannot reach dl.google.com, where the emulator downloads its jar. Treat test/emulator/rtdb.test.js as UNVERIFIED CODE and expect its first real run to need harness fixes. Where the emulator disagrees with targaryen, THE EMULATOR IS RIGHT.
STILL NOT COVERED BY ANY OF THEM: the api/ endpoints with real credentials (needs a staging Firebase project - never point an integration test at production), Agora voice, Cloudinary and Firebase Storage uploads, and NSFW scanning against Nyckel. Each needs a third-party account.
comments.migrations: All optional, all additive, none required for v54.6. PRIVACY: scripts/migrate_privacy.js moves real email addresses out of users/ into userPrivate/; verify with scripts/verify_privacy.js; DO NOT use --clear-source or --rollback without reading the EXIT CODES table at the top of scripts/rollback.js first. AVATARS: scripts/add_rules_avatars.py then scripts/migrate_avatars.js move inline avatars to avatars/$id - a sign-in used to download about 18 MB because they were stored inline. Back up first: the JSON export is the only way back. scripts/estimate_quota.js sizes it before you commit to it.
comments.history:
v54.4 gave site owners the power to delete any server and fixed the nine side-node paths the delete had always been refused on. v54.5 took the site-owner grant away again. v54.6 RESTORED it in the client, the rules and the server menu, and stopped Discover reading a member count that was copied into the listing the day a server was published and never updated.
v54.7 finished the invite system. Invite LINKS were not unfinished - inviteUrl() and the boot handler both existed - they were BROKEN: handleInviteLink() resolved a code at invites/$code when invites live at invites/$sid/$code, so every link anybody ever opened said 'invalid or expired', and the UI had been changed to say 'coming soon' to match the symptom rather than the cause being found. v54.7 also made redemption atomic (the old counter could be beaten by two people clicking at once, making a 1-use invite effectively unlimited), rebuilt the permission matrix to batch its writes, added the owner control center and a secure path for granting global custom roles, and fixed a model/rules disagreement where a non-member was granted the @everyone DEFAULTS for any server the client had no data about.
comments.v546-notes: Three things worth knowing before changing this release. (1) DModel.basePerms() answers 'what can this person DO' and folds site ownership in; DModel.storedPerms() answers 'what do their real role assignments grant' and deliberately does not. Only storedPerms is written to serverMembers/$sid/$uid/p, because that cache would otherwise outlive the ownership that justified it. (2) DModel.holdServer()/holdServerReady() temporarily attach a server the viewer has not joined, for a site owner managing somebody else's; nothing holds one by default, so ordinary members pay nothing. (3) Discover's counts come from per-server serverMembers listeners held only while the pane is open.
comments.markdown: v54.6 removed every .md file from the project on purpose. Anything that was worth keeping is in this "comments" object, in the header comment of the script it describes, or in the code it documents. Please do not reintroduce loose documentation files - put the explanation next to the thing it explains.
comments.targaryen: An implementation of the Realtime Database rules language, used by the rules suites. It is NOT Google's evaluator - see SECURITY-TEST-RESULTS.md. Pinned to a major version because the API differs between 3.x and 4.x: 3.x takes database(rules, data, now).as({uid}), and update() takes `now` as its THIRD argument while write() takes it as its FOURTH. Getting that wrong makes clock comparisons silently fail.
comments.playwright: Drives real Chrome for the browser suites. Only test/run-*.js need it; every test/security/*.js suite runs without it.
comments.no-dependencies: The site has no runtime dependencies. Firebase is loaded from the CDN by js/loader.js, exactly as before - nothing here changes how the site loads or is hosted.
comments.v547-notes:
Worth knowing before changing this release.
(1) INVITES. DModel.previewInvite() READS ONLY - opening a link, or three people opening the same link out of a group chat, cannot spend a use. DModel.reserveInviteUse() is the only thing that spends one, inside a runTransaction that re-checks expiry and the limit on every attempt, so the decision and the increment are one indivisible step. The use is reserved BEFORE the join: if the join then fails the use is spent, which is the safe direction - the rules let a member increment `uses` and nothing else, so a decrement is impossible, and the other ordering is the unlimited-invite bug.
(2) PERMISSIONS. basePerms() answers 'what can this person DO' and folds site ownership in; storedPerms() answers 'what do their real role assignments grant' and deliberately does not. Only storedPerms is written to serverMembers/$sid/$uid/p, because that cache would otherwise outlive the ownership that justified it. Both now return {} for a non-member of a non-ICH server.
(3) The permission matrix holds its changes and writes ONCE. Every toggle used to write immediately, and each write re-flattens the permission cache for EVERY member - so editing twelve permissions in a 200-member server fired twelve cascades of two hundred writes, and a half-finished edit was already live.
(4) DModel.holdServer()/holdServerReady() temporarily attach a server the viewer has not joined, for a site owner managing somebody else's. Nothing holds one by default.
(5) The owner control center reads servers/ and serverMembers/ ONCE with get(), never with a listener, and only when opened - a site owner reading them downloads every server record.
(6) PERM_CATS was regrouped into General/Membership/Messaging/Moderation/Voice/Advanced. Only the grouping moved: not one permission key changed, was added or was removed, so the rules (which name every key in two places) and every existing role record are untouched.
comments.api:
Endpoints and what each needs. All POST-only except /api/health (GET or POST) and /api/ipcheck (GET or POST).
  attest, tos, login, spin, totaward, totmilestone, ipban  -> FIREBASE_SA
  ipcheck      -> IP_HASH_SALT (required; without it answers 503 'unconfigured', naming the variable - NOT a 500, because a missing variable stays broken until somebody sets it while a 500 invites a pointless retry). VPN_API_KEY is optional on top.
  nsfw         -> NYCKEL_CLIENT_ID + NYCKEL_CLIENT_SECRET + NYCKEL_FUNCTION_ID. Unconfigured is reported as unconfigured and NEVER as 'clean' - claiming an unscanned image was scanned is worse than saying scanning is off.
  customrole   -> FIREBASE_SA. Site owners only, checked with an admin read. NEW in v54.7.
  health       -> nothing. Unauthenticated ON PURPOSE, so the diagnostics panel works when signing in is the thing that is broken. That is only safe because the body is exactly 'which services exist and whether each is configured', as booleans. If a field is ever added that is not safe for an anonymous caller, it needs an owner check first - and is probably the wrong idea. NEW in v54.7.
